relationship: Sending a message in shared-key or public/private-key mode connects key roles to the readable and encrypted states of traffic.

learnerLoop.action: Choose a mode, edit the message and transmit it.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The message becomes packet traffic with keys assigned to the selected mode.
learnerLoop.evidence: Source and cipher previews, key labels, stations and wire state show the transmission.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Compare who can use a key or read the message in the other mode.

invariants: The visible key roles match the selected encryption mode.
The cipher preview and traffic represent the current message.
safeAdaptations: Change messages, scenarios or explanatory prompts while preserving the contrast between shared and public/private keys.

task.description: Key-method goal and persistent confidentiality question/outcomes above the canvas.
task.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

model.description: Message, encryption gate, shared-line stream and endpoint decryption.
model.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

keys.description: Large key-shaped SVG artwork stays the same in the tray, drag preview and device bay; tokens own the first-interaction hint.
keys.visibility: Only the key trays for the active method are visible.

evidence.description: Readable plaintext, wire contents, endpoint results and up to four persistent captures; canvas height grows to contain Eve.
evidence.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

message.description: Plain text and its transmitted representation.
message.domain: Text converted by this lab’s illustrative cipher.
message.output: Shared line, Bob output and Eve captures.

key-placement.description: Key ownership at sender, Bob and Eve.
key-placement.domain: Shared K7 copies or Bob public/private tokens.
key-placement.output: Bays, decrypt results and confidentiality indicators.

modes.shared: All K7 tokens are copies of one secret; the same secret encrypts and decrypts.
modes.asymmetric: Bob’s public key encrypts; his private key decrypts.
modes.support: No Working or exam toggle. Changing method resets its transmission/key setup; successful method marks are retained.

dependencies: No sender key sends plain text; a private key at the asymmetric sender is rejected.
Eve may decrypt stored captures when later given a suitable key.
The three goal indicators derive from wire protection and endpoint readability.
implementation.completion: A method is recorded successful when the line is protected, Bob reads and Eve cannot. Both methods remain replayable.
limitations: Cipher is illustrative, not a secure cryptographic algorithm.
The fixed-geometry device board fits its available width; dense device annotations remain smaller on phones.
